newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian fruit exports to Taiwan grow - Fischer.
newsitem.headline: Australian fruit exports to Taiwan grow - Fischer.

text.p: Australian exporters had been quick to take advantage of amended Taiwanese regulations which allow entry for Australian stone and citrus fruits, Australia's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade Tim Fischer said.
The changes, which allow first time access for peaches, plums, oranges, lemons and grapefruit, are party of a World Trade Organisation (WTO) package struck in October last year,
About 1,000 tonnes of Australian peaches and plums were shipped to Taiwan earlier this year under the terms of the agreement, Fischer said.
Australia has new access for 600 tonnes of cirtus fruit and shipments would start soon.
In addition to the first-time access, Australia's yearly apple quota had been doubled to 2,400 tonnes, he said.
In total, the increased access for Australian fruit to Taiwan's market was worth about A$10 million, up from Australia's 1996 fruit exports to Taiwan of about A$5 million.
Taiwan's latest action follows its reduction of beef tariffs earlier this month, also under the WTO package of agreements.
This provided an initial cut of A$3 a kilogram in the tariff faced by Australian beef.
